newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria bans temporary tobacco, alcohol imports.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria bans temporary tobacco, alcohol imports.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim cabinet decided on Thursday to ban temporary imports of alcohol and tobacco in a bid to curb excise duty evasion as part of an International Monetary Fund (IMF) funding accord.
"Tobacco and alcohol imports arranged as temporary imports should be cancelled by the time the decision takes effect," a government spokeswoman told reporters.
The decision comes into force three months after being published in the State Gazette.
"It is possible to enforce the ban immediately but restricting trade in Bulgaria's numerous duty free trade zones will take some time," a finance ministry official said.

Some local businessmen declare large shipments of beverages and cigarettes intended for sale inside the country as temporary import destined for export to third countries to avoid paying high excise duties.
Excise duties on spirits are up to 50 percent and on tobacco 40 percent.

Boosting tax revenue by restricting free trade zones and banning temporary imports is part of a list of actions the interim cabinet is expected to complete before the IMF executive board meets to consider disbursing the first tranche of a standby accord on April 11.

Under the $510 million 14-month accord agreed last month Bulgaria pledged to introduce a fixed exchange rate system known as a currency board in June to restore confidence in its collapsing financial system. -- Sofia Newsroom, +3592-9814145
